name: Ya'rubid dynasty
alt: Imamate of Oman under the Ya'rubids

successors.name: Sultanate of Oman
successors.text: Oman under Ahmad bin Said, elected imam in 1744 and victorious over Bal'arab bin Himyar in the second half of 1749; Cliopatria's Sultanate of Oman shape of 1744 already includes the Swahili coast

ledger.x: 1624: Nasir bin Murshid founds the Ya'rubid imamate of Oman at Nizwa.
1633: Nasir bin Murshid expels the Portuguese from Julfar.
1643: the Omanis take the fort at Sohar from the Portuguese.
1650: the Portuguese are expelled from Oman.
1696: the Omanis besiege Fort Jesus at Mombasa.
1698: Fort Jesus falls and the Swahili coast with it.
1698: the siege ends on 13 December with the surrender of Fort Jesus.
March 1737: a Persian force arrives in Oman.
1743: the Ya'rubid hold on the coast ends with the loss of Muscat; the Persians stay until 1747.
1744: the Swahili coast passes to the Al Bu Said.

wars.name: Omani-Portuguese conflicts
wars.outcome: The Portuguese lose their holdings in Oman (1650) and Mombasa (1698); Mombasa leaves Omani hands in 1728.

wars.name: Siege of Fort Jesus (1696-1698)
wars.outcome: Omani victory after 33 months: the fort surrenders on 13 December 1698 and the whole coast of Kenya and Tanzania with Zanzibar and Pemba falls to the Omanis.

wars.name: Ya'rubid civil war (1718-1724)
wars.outcome: A succession dispute after 1718 turns into a civil war in which Muhammad bin Nasir seizes power (1724-1728); no frontier changes on the pages opened.

wars.name: Persian intervention in Oman (1737-1747)
wars.outcome: A Persian force arrives in March 1737 at the call of Saif bin Sultan II; Persian troops return in 1742, take Muscat in 1743 and besiege Sohar; Ahmad bin Said, confirmed governor of Sohar and Barka, is elected imam in 1744 and in 1747 massacres the remaining…

wars.name: Ahmad bin Said's war against Bal'arab bin Himyar (1749)
wars.outcome: In the second half of 1749 Ahmad's army defeats and kills Bal'arab near Jebel Akhdar: the end of Ya'rubid power.

certainty.note: Tribal interior and coastal forts: no treaty lines; the Portuguese enclaves (Julfar to 1633, Sohar to 1643, Muscat to 1650, Mombasa to 1698) are points, not frontiers.

sources.title: Ahmad bin Said (Abu Hilal Ahmad bin Said)
